sub_unit_name: Types of corrosion: Galvanic, water-line and pitting corrosion

content.title: Types of Corrosion
content.description: Corrosion occurs in different forms depending on the environment and the nature of the metal. Common types include galvanic corrosion, water-line corrosion, and pitting corrosion.

content.content: Different types of corrosion affect engineering materials in different ways. Identifying the type of corrosion helps in selecting suitable preventive measures and improving the service life of metal components.

content.title: Importance
content.content: Understanding the types of corrosion helps prevent equipment failure, reduce maintenance costs, and improve safety.

Galvanic corrosion occurs when two dissimilar metals are electrically connected in the presence of an electrolyte. The more active metal acts as the anode and corrodes, while the less active metal acts as the cathode and is protected.
Water-line corrosion occurs at the junction of water and air due to differences in oxygen concentration. The region just below the water level becomes anodic and undergoes corrosion.
Pitting corrosion is a localized form of corrosion that produces small pits or holes on the metal surface. It is dangerous because it causes severe damage while affecting only a small area.

right_points: Water-line: Due to oxygen concentration difference

items.question: Galvanic Corrosion
items.answer: Avoid direct contact between dissimilar metals or use insulation.

items.question: Water-line Corrosion
items.answer: Apply protective coatings and maintain uniform oxygen distribution.

items.question: Pitting Corrosion
items.answer: Use corrosion-resistant alloys and avoid chloride-rich environments.

items.question: General Protection
items.answer: Use coatings, inhibitors, cathodic protection, and proper material selection.

content.title: Engineering Significance
content.content: Pitting corrosion is considered one of the most dangerous forms because it is difficult to detect and can lead to sudden equipment failure.

content.title: Quick Revision
points: Galvanic corrosion occurs between dissimilar metals.
Water-line corrosion is caused by differential aeration.
Pitting corrosion creates small but deep pits.
Proper protection methods increase the life of engineering materials.
